get.description: Retrieve a page of CRM objects of a specified type. You can control the data returned by specifying properties, associations, and whether to include archived records. This endpoint supports pagination to navigate through large sets of data.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The paging cursor token of the last successfully read resource will be returned as the `paging.next.after` JSON property of a paged response containing more results.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived.

parameters.name: associations
parameters.description: A comma separated list of object types to retrieve associated IDs for. If any of the specified associations do not exist, they will be ignored.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of results to display per page.

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned in the response. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored.

parameters.name: propertiesWithHistory
parameters.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned along with their history of previous values. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored. Usage of this parameter will reduce the maximum number of objects that can be read by a single request.

post.description: Create a CRM object with the specified properties and receive a copy of the object, including its ID. This endpoint is useful for adding new objects to your CRM system. Documentation and examples for creating standard objects are provided.

Location.description: URL of the newly created resource

post.description: Archive a batch of CRM objects by their IDs. This operation moves the specified objects to the recycling bin, effectively archiving them. It is useful for managing large sets of data that are no longer needed in active use but may be required for record-keeping purposes.

Create a batch of CRM objects with specified properties in your HubSpot account. This endpoint allows you to efficiently create multiple objects in a single request, returning a copy of each created object, including their IDs. This is useful for bulk data entry or migration tasks.

Retrieve a batch of CRM objects by their internal IDs or unique property values. This endpoint is useful for fetching multiple objects in a single request, allowing for efficient data retrieval. The response includes the objects' details, and you can specify whether to include archived objects.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived.

post.description: Update a batch of CRM objects in your HubSpot account. This endpoint allows you to modify multiple objects at once by providing their details in the request body. It's useful for bulk updates where you need to change properties across several objects efficiently.

Create or update a batch of CRM objects by their unique property values. This endpoint is useful for synchronizing data where some objects may already exist and others need to be created. The operation will return a response indicating the success or failure of each object upserted.

Permanently delete a contact and all associated content to comply with GDPR regulations. This operation can identify a contact by their email address if the optional 'idProperty' is set to 'email'. If the email address is not found, it will be added to a blocklist to prevent future use.

Merge two CRM objects of the same type in your HubSpot account. This operation combines the properties and associations of the specified objects into a single object. Use this endpoint to consolidate duplicate records or unify data under a primary object.

Search CRM objects of a specified type using various filters and criteria. This endpoint allows you to perform complex queries to retrieve CRM objects based on specific properties or conditions. It is useful for finding objects that meet certain criteria within your HubSpot account.

get.description: Read an object identified by `objectId`. By default, `objectId` refers to the internal object ID, but it can also refer to any unique property value specified by the `idProperty` query parameter. You can control the data returned by specifying the `properties` query parameter.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived.

parameters.name: associations
parameters.description: A comma separated list of object types to retrieve associated IDs for. If any of the specified associations do not exist, they will be ignored.

parameters.name: idProperty
parameters.description: The name of a property whose values are unique for this object type

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned in the response. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored.

parameters.name: propertiesWithHistory
parameters.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned along with their history of previous values. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored.

delete.description: Move an Object identified by `{objectId}` to the recycling bin. This operation effectively archives the specified object, making it no longer active but still recoverable from the recycling bin.

patch.description: Perform a partial update of an Object identified by `{objectId}`. `{objectId}` refers to the internal object ID by default, or optionally any unique property value as specified by the `idProperty` query param. Provided property values will be overwritten. Read-only and non-existent properties will be ignored. Properties values can be cleared by passing an empty string.

parameters.description: The name of a property whose values are unique for this object type

put.description: Create the default association type between two specified object types in the CRM. This endpoint is useful for establishing a basic relationship between objects, such as linking a contact with a company or a deal. It requires specifying both the source and target object types and their respective IDs.
